item: A ratchet on the buttons that reach the network: each asks first or names the kill-switch refusal (invariant 14, R292 C3)
refs: PR #1542; R292 C3; osm-lane consent sweep item 1
summary: tests/test_consent_coverage.py holds a table of the UI actions whose server handler fetches. A row is consent (the client function calls ensureOnline or ensureAiEgress in its own body; there are TWO consent functions) or named (nothing asked, because the kill switch already stops every byte; the refusal must be NAMED, proved by a real refusal with the kill switch engaged). Discovery is the other direction: every src/api route handler that names get_fetcher, make_fetcher, following_fetcher, EthicalFetcher or WikiClient must be a row, and every discovered row must still be found, zero slack, so a new egress route cannot ship silent. Two feed-verification rows are kind gap: a KNOWN defect pinned as it is (offline it stores an unreachable verdict and a ladder attempt for a healthy feed and the toast says Checked.), so fixing it is a visible edit of the table. The consent check reads code, not prose (comments stripped, an awaited call before the first api request). 13 mutants killed. Its building corrected the sweep: importCustomFeed has no ensureOnline (10 unprompted egress buttons, not 9) and refreshStatSubs is named, not consented. Limit: discovery is by direct reference in the handler body; helpers (stats refresh, weather) are hand-listed rows pinned by their own tests.
